description: RAM disks that allocate memory on demand and free it on TRIM, and disk-image mounting, on the Arsenal Image Mounter driver (the successor to ImDisk Toolkit)
notes: Installed by upstream's own installer: in Program Files\AIM Toolkit, unless an earlier
installation chose another folder (its Apps & features entry says which), with the
Arsenal Image Mounter driver, RamDyn, RamDiskUI and MountImg. It sets up no services
until RamDiskUI saves a RAM disk.
RAM disks: RamDyn.exe in that folder prints its syntax when run without arguments. It
is the process that holds a disk's memory, so the disk lasts as long as it runs.
scoop uninstall removes the driver, and with it every disk it serves. scoop update
installs over the old version instead, leaving the driver and its disks alone.
x64 only: the driver has no ARM64 build.
pre_install: # The zip holds files.cab and upstream's install.bat, which unpacks the cab with
# extrac32 and runs config.exe, the installer, from what it unpacked. The unpacking
# is done here with the same extrac32, into $dir, for the installer below.
# Start-Process -Wait, since extrac32 is a GUI program PowerShell would not wait for.
if (!(Test-Path "$dir\config.exe") -or !(Test-Path "$dir\driver\Win10\phdskmnt.inf")) { error "$app`: extrac32 did not unpack files.cab into $dir"; break }

script: # config.exe always relaunches itself through the runas verb and waits for that
# copy, so this is one UAC prompt, and -Wait covers the whole installation.
# A fresh install selects every component and the desktop shortcuts; an upgrade
# keeps the earlier choices and folder. RamDiskUI's component, which also brings
# RamDyn, is forced on; Explorer's menu entries and desktop shortcuts are forced
# off. MountImg is left to the default: config.exe reads /mountimg:'s digit one
# character too far, so /mountimg:0 would not do what it says.
# A file in use, such as a RamDyn serving a RAM disk, is renamed aside and deleted
# at the next reboot, and the new one copied in: the running disk carries on.
Start-Process -FilePath "$dir\config.exe" -ArgumentList '/fullsilent', '/ramdiskui:1', '/menu_entries:0', '/shortcuts_desktop:0' -Wait -Verb RunAs
# config.exe exits 0 whatever happened, a declined UAC prompt included, so what it
# left is checked: its uninstall entry at this version, and the driver's service.
$entry = Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\AIM-tk' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

if (!$entry -or $entry.DisplayVersion -ne $version -or !(Get-Service phdskmnt -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { error "$app`: config.exe did not install AIM Toolkit $version; was the UAC prompt declined?"; break }
# scoop update runs the old version's uninstaller before the new version's
# installer. /silentuninstall removes the driver, and with it every disk it
# serves, a RAM disk holding %TEMP% included; config.exe upgrades in place without
# it. So only an uninstall runs it. $cmd is the scoop subcommand being run.
if ($cmd -eq 'update') { return }
$entry = Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\AIM-tk' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (!$entry -or !(Test-Path -LiteralPath $entry.DisplayIcon)) { warn "$app`: no AIM Toolkit installation found to uninstall"; return }
# The installed config.exe, as /silentuninstall requires; DisplayIcon names it.
Start-Process -FilePath $entry.DisplayIcon -ArgumentList '/silentuninstall' -Wait -Verb RunAs
